condition: I'm looking for products that serve similar purposes, regardless of their brand or category.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Product descriptions can indicate what products are used for, directly supporting purpose-based similarity independent of brand or category. The path supplies only products reviewed by a customer.
Product descriptions can indicate intended purpose, directly supporting comparisons of products regardless of brand or category.
Product titles can directly indicate what a product is for, supporting comparisons by purpose without relying on brand or category; titles may not fully describe intended use.

The review.product_id path reaches product.description, a product-level field that can provide evidence of products’ purposes without relying on brand or category; the schema does not specify what the descriptions contain.
Product titles can provide direct clues about what products are for, and the review-to-product path supplies those titles; the schema does not guarantee that titles state purpose explicitly.
Product titles may describe product functions or intended uses, supporting purpose-based similarity without relying on brand or category; the path limits signals to products reviewed by a customer.
Product review text may describe uses or purposes, providing relevant but indirect evidence for finding products with similar functions.
Review summaries linked to each product may provide clues about its use or purpose, independent of brand or category, but they are indirect and not an explicit product-purpose attribute.

Review summaries may describe what reviewed products are used for, which can help identify similar purposes; the customer-to-review path only provides summaries of that customer's reviews, not a direct product-to-product similarity link.
Customer review text may indirectly describe product uses, but this path supplies no direct product-purpose attribute or product endpoint.
Reviewed products' categories may weakly suggest their purposes, but the condition explicitly disregards category, and this path only connects a customer to products they reviewed.
The path links customers to products they reviewed, and price may provide weak indirect context, but price does not indicate product purpose or similarity.
Products connect to customers through reviews, so customer names may provide an indirect association between products, but they do not describe product purpose.
Review text may mention how a product is used, but it is indirect evidence of product purpose and the signal path does not include product attributes.
Review summaries may mention a product’s use or purpose, but they are indirect evidence and the stated path does not connect reviews to product records.
The path links customers to products they reviewed, which may weakly associate products reviewed by the same customer, but it provides no direct evidence that the products serve similar purposes.
Products connected through shared reviewing customers may be indirectly associated, but this path does not encode product purpose; brand and category are explicitly irrelevant.
Reviews linked to the same customer provide a weak behavioral association, but this path contains no product-purpose information to establish similarity.
The path links reviews to their products, but the relationship alone provides no evidence that different products serve similar purposes.
Price may weakly indicate comparable products, but it provides no direct evidence of their purpose.
The path connects reviews to their products and exposes product.price, which may weakly suggest comparable product types, but price does not directly indicate purpose.
Product category may weakly indicate purpose, but the condition explicitly allows matches across categories, so category alone is poor evidence of similarity.
The path identifies customers associated with reviews, which may weakly connect reviewed products through a shared customer, but customer names provide no evidence about product purpose.
The path reaches products and exposes their category, but the condition explicitly says to ignore category; it provides little evidence for similarity of purpose.
The path links a product to its reviews, but that association alone does not indicate which products serve similar purposes.
The path links customers to reviews, but verified status does not indicate product purpose or similarity.
Customer names provide no schema-grounded evidence about product purpose or similarity.
The path provides customers’ review ratings, which do not indicate products’ purposes or whether those purposes are similar.
Review times on the customer-to-review path provide no schema-grounded evidence about product purposes or similarity.
The path yields brands of products reviewed by a customer, but brand is explicitly irrelevant to the condition and provides no evidence about product purpose.
Product brand is explicitly irrelevant to the condition, which seeks similar purposes regardless of brand.
Product review ratings provide no schema-grounded evidence about products’ purposes or functional similarity.
Review times are linked to products, but the schema provides no indication that review timing reveals product purpose or similarity.
Verified status indicates whether a product’s reviews are verified, but does not describe product purpose or connect products with similar uses.
Review ratings indicate reviewers’ evaluations, not the products’ purposes or functional similarity.
Review time provides temporal information, but no schema link indicates product purpose or similarity.
A review's verified status does not indicate the product's purpose or similarity to other products.
The path reaches reviewed products, but brand is explicitly irrelevant to the condition and does not indicate product purpose.
The path connects customers to their reviews, but does not connect products or provide evidence that products serve similar purposes.

condition: Which products appeal to similar customers based on their reviewing behavior?

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The path connects each product to the customers who reviewed it, directly supporting comparison of products by shared reviewers.

The customer→review→product path links each customer to products they reviewed, and product.title identifies those products. This is strong evidence of reviewing behavior for comparing customer overlap, though it does not include review ratings or other behavior details.
The customer–review–product path directly links customers to the products they reviewed, enabling comparison of product overlap across customers.

The path links each customer’s reviews to the reviewed products’ brands, giving a useful basis for comparing customers’ brand-level reviewing behavior, though it does not capture other review or product attributes.

The path links each product to the names of customers who reviewed it, so shared names can indicate overlapping reviewers. It does not capture other aspects of reviewing behavior, such as ratings or review timing.

The path links customers to products they reviewed, and product.category can indicate whether their reviewed products share categories. It is useful for identifying broad similarities in reviewing behavior, but does not distinguish products within a category or capture review ratings.

The customer-to-review-to-product path links customers with products they reviewed, providing behavioral association evidence; product descriptions add product-content context but do not directly measure overlap in reviewing behavior.

Customer-linked review ratings provide evidence about customers’ rating behavior, but the path does not connect those ratings to products, so it is incomplete for identifying products that appeal to similar customers.
Review text can reveal customers’ opinions and preferences from their reviewing behavior, but the stated path does not connect those reviews to specific products.
Review summaries can provide evidence about customers’ expressed preferences, but the stated path does not connect those reviews to products, so product-level similarity is incomplete.
Review text provides evidence of what customers say about each product, which can help compare reviewing behavior, but this path does not identify or link reviewers across products.
Review ratings provide evidence of customers’ product assessments, but the signal alone does not identify which customer or product each rating belongs to for comparison.
Review text provides direct evidence of what customers say about reviewed products, but alone it does not identify customers or compare their reviewing behavior across products.
Categories of products reached from reviews can indicate what kinds of products are reviewed, but this signal does not connect reviews to customers or show overlap in customers across products.

Descriptions of products linked to reviews can support comparing the kinds of products reviewed, but this path does not connect reviews to customers or directly establish which customers reviewed them.
Product titles identify the items associated with reviews, which can help compare reviewed products, but the stated path does not connect reviews to customers.
Links reviews to the products being reviewed, which supports analyzing product review behavior; it does not connect reviews to customers, so similarity between customers is not established.
Product-linked review summaries can indicate what customers discuss or value, but this path does not identify customers or show which customers review multiple products.
Brands of reviewed products can provide a limited clue to reviewing preferences, but this path does not connect reviews to customers or establish which customers reviewed each product.

The product–review relationship identifies reviews associated with each product, which is relevant to reviewing behavior, but this path does not connect reviews to customers for comparing customer overlap.

Review times can provide a limited signal of customers’ reviewing behavior, but this path does not connect reviews to products, so it cannot directly identify which products similar customers reviewed.

Verified status is available on each customer's reviews and offers a weak behavioral signal, but the path does not connect those reviews to products, so it cannot directly identify products reviewed by similar customers.
The path connects customers to products they reviewed, and product.price can weakly characterize those products; it does not directly capture shared reviewing behavior or customer similarity.
Brand can weakly group products that may appeal to similar customers, but this signal has no path to customer or review behavior.
Product category can provide weak context for grouping products, but it does not capture customer identities or review behavior needed to determine which products share reviewers.
Product descriptions may indirectly help identify products with similar content, but this signal does not capture which customers reviewed them or their reviewing behavior.
Product price is available and may be a weak proxy for customer appeal, but it does not capture the customer–product reviewing relationships needed to identify similar customers.
Product-linked review ratings provide weak evidence of how reviewers evaluate each product, but this path does not identify or compare the customers reviewing different products.
Review times can indicate when each product was reviewed, offering weak behavioral evidence, but this path does not connect products to reviewers or show whether they share customers.
A product’s review verified statuses provide limited evidence about its reviewing behavior, but do not identify customers or link customers across products to establish similarity.
Review time can provide a weak behavioral cue about when reviews are written, but it does not identify customer overlap or connect reviews to products on the stated path.
Review summaries may weakly indicate customer interests, but this signal alone does not connect products to shared customers or capture their reviewing patterns.
Verified status is a review-level attribute and may weakly characterize reviewing behavior, but it does not identify customers or directly establish which products they review.
Customer names identify who wrote a review, but the stated path does not link those reviewers to products, so it provides only indirect evidence of which products share customers.

Prices of products linked to reviews can weakly indicate customer product preferences, but price alone does not establish which customers reviewed the same products or how their reviewing behavior is similar.
The path connects customers to their reviews, providing indirect evidence of reviewing behavior, but it does not connect those reviews to products.

Links reviews to the customers who wrote them, offering indirect evidence about reviewer overlap; the path does not connect reviews to products, which is needed to identify which products those customers reviewed.
Product titles can identify products for comparison, but they do not show which customers reviewed them or reveal overlap in reviewing behavior.
Customer names can identify reviewers, but the signal contains no reviewing behavior or product associations needed to find products reviewed by similar customers.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review text is directly connected to each product through review.product_id and can contain descriptions of its strengths and weaknesses.
Review text is a direct source of written feedback that can describe a product’s strengths and weaknesses.

Review text can directly describe a review’s product strengths and weaknesses, and the customer-to-review path reaches those reviews. The path does not include the product relationship, so product-specific linkage is incomplete.
The product-to-review relationship reaches reviews, and review.summary can provide concise evidence about a product’s strengths and weaknesses.
A review’s summary is directly associated with the review and may concisely capture insights, but the schema does not establish that it covers both strengths and weaknesses.
Review summaries are directly relevant text for identifying strengths and weaknesses, but the stated path only connects customers to their reviews and does not connect those reviews to a product.
Ratings on a product’s reviews can indicate overall positive or negative assessments, but do not provide detailed explanations of strengths or weaknesses.
A review’s rating can indicate overall positive or negative sentiment, but it does not describe specific product strengths or weaknesses.
The direct product-to-review relationship identifies reviews for a product, but the relationship alone does not indicate whether they discuss strengths or weaknesses.
Ratings on a customer's reviews can indicate positive or negative sentiment, but they do not reveal specific product strengths or weaknesses; the signal also does not connect to the product.
The product-to-review path reaches reviews, and their verified attribute may help indicate review credibility, but it does not directly describe product strengths or weaknesses.
The path connects customers to their reviews and exposes review.verified, which may offer indirect context, but it does not indicate whether a review describes product strengths or weaknesses.

The path connects customers to products they reviewed, and product.description may provide context for interpreting a review. It does not directly indicate whether the review describes strengths or weaknesses.

Review rating directly signals customer satisfaction and perceived quality, but the review-only path provides no price evidence for assessing balance.
